To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a tool for the exploration of the chemical space can support the identification of new compounds for further testing, (2) a tool can be used to identify compounds with similar properties, (3) the tool can support the analysis of structure activity relationships (SAR), (4) the tool can be used in a collaborative manner.

(i) a flexible and interactive exploration of large chemical spaces is possible through the use of a projection mechanism that is guided by one or a few molecules of interest; (ii) the use of the projection mechanism in the exploration of large libraries allows the biologist and the chemist to quickly identify the most promising molecules for further investigation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the exploration of the chemical space of large compound libraries, and the analysis of the structure-activity relationships of the molecules in a chemical library.
the exploration of large compound libraries, and the development of a visualization tool that allows biologists to analyze and interpret large compound screens.
the development of a tool for the exploration of high-throughput screening data that supports the analysis of large libraries of compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tool is a useful tool for the analysis, exploration and interpretation of high-throughput screening data.
our approach provides a flexible and powerful tool that can support the exploration of large libraries, and can be used to support the analysis of large scale chemical screens.
HiTSEE is an effective tool for the exploration of chemical spaces, and the visualization of the relationships among the compounds in the space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HiTSEE provides the user with an intuitive interface to explore large chemical spaces and to navigate through the results of high-throughput screening (HTS) experiments.
we have developed a tool to support the exploration of large libraries of molecules, with a focus on the analysis of SAR and chemical neighborhoods.

we have developed an interactive visualization tool for high-throughput screening (HTS) experiments, which supports biologists in the analysis of chemical libraries and the identification of potential drug candidates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a flexible interaction mechanism is needed to support the analysis of large data sets and that the use of a single molecule of interest as an anchor point is a powerful mechanism to navigate through large chemical spaces.

a flexible tool that supports a wide range of interaction techniques is needed in order to support the analysis of large screening experiments and to provide an effective means to support hypothesis generation and the discovery of new chemical scaffolds.
, while a large amount of chemical data is available, the ability to navigate and explore it is still a major challenge.
